subject: Literacy
title: Print around us
objectives: Children will notice print on signs, labels and books.
Children will recognise their own name card with support.
content: Noticing print on signs, labels and books, recognising their own name card, and looking at print in books.
teachingActivities: Point to print as you talk about it; walk around the school to find signs; always say what a sign says; make children’s name cards with a photo and write names in clear lower-case letters with a capital first letter.
learnerActivities: Notice print around them, say what it is for and find their own name card among three.
resources: A "STOP" sign, an "EXIT" sign and a toilet sign
assessment: Observe whether each child points to print and finds their own name card among three.
expectedOutcomes: Points to print and says what it is for.
Finds their own name card among three.
crossCurricular: Understanding the World: signs in the community

lessons.title: Words on signs
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will notice print on signs and say what a sign is for.
successCriteria: Says what the sign tells us
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can handle books, name pictures and recognise their own name card with a photo.
resources: A STOP sign, an EXIT sign and a toilet sign
lessons.starter: Show a STOP sign and say "This sign says STOP. It tells us to stop." Hold up a hand.
teacherActivities: Show each sign and say what it says: "This says STOP. This says EXIT."
Walk around the school to find signs.
Stop at each sign and ask "What does it say?"
Return to class and talk about the signs.
learnerActivities: Children look and point to the words.
Children walk and point to signs.
Child points or says the word.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each sign and say what it says: "This says STOP. This says EXIT." Children: Children look and point to the words.
Step 2. Teacher: Walk around the school to find signs. Children: Children walk and point to signs.
Step 3. Teacher: Stop at each sign and ask "What does it say?" Children: Child points or says the word.
Step 4. Teacher: Return to class and talk about the signs. Children: Child names a sign.

practical.title: Sign walk
steps: Walk around the school in a line.
Stop at each sign and talk about it.
practical.safety: Walk in a line with an adult at the front and the back, away from traffic. Hold hands at doors and steps.

differentiation.support: Hold hands and point to the sign together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a sign at home and tell a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What is the sign for?
questions.expected: It tells us what to do.

expectedOutcomes: Says what a sign is for
lessons.conclusion: Say "Stop" with a raised hand and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Point out signs on the road or in the market and say what they say.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "notice print on signs and say what a sign is for" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Labels and packets
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will notice print on food and toy packets.
successCriteria: Points to print on a packet
Names the item from the label
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can handle books, name pictures and recognise their own name card with a photo.
resources: Empty clean food packets and tins
lessons.starter: Hold up an empty milk tin and say "Look, there are words on this tin. It says milk."
teacherActivities: Show each packet and point to the words. Say what it says.
Say "Where are the words?" and wait.
Ask "What is it?" and let children name the item.
Let each child pick a packet and tell a friend.
learnerActivities: Child shows and says the name.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each packet and point to the words. Say what it says. Children: Children point to the words.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Where are the words?" and wait. Children: Child points to the print.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "What is it?" and let children name the item. Children: Child names the item.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child pick a packet and tell a friend. Children: Child shows and says the name.

practical.title: Label shop
steps: Set up a pretend shop with clean empty packets.
Children point to the print on each packet.
practical.safety: Use only clean, empty, undamaged packets with no sharp edges. Wash hands after handling and do not use real food.

differentiation.support: Point to the words together and say the item name.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a packet with a picture and words.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What is this?
questions.expected: Milk, rice or the item named.

expectedOutcomes: Points to print on a label
lessons.conclusion: Put the packets back and say goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Show your child words on packets at home and read them aloud.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "notice print on food and toy packets" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: My name card
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will find their own name card among three.
successCriteria: Points to their own name card
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can handle books, name pictures and recognise their own name card with a photo.
lessons.starter: Hold up a name card and say "This says Tola. This is Tola’s card." Ask "Whose card is this?"
teacherActivities: Show each card and say the name. Point to the photo and the word.
Put three cards on the floor and ask each child to find their own.
Cover the photo with your thumb and ask again.
Let each child hold their card and show it to a friend.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the name.
Child recognises the card by the word or first letter.
Child holds up the card and says their name.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each card and say the name. Point to the photo and the word. Children: Children look and say the name.
Step 2. Teacher: Put three cards on the floor and ask each child to find their own. Children: Child points to their card.
Step 3. Teacher: Cover the photo with your thumb and ask again. Children: Child recognises the card by the word or first letter.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child hold their card and show it to a friend. Children: Child holds up the card and says their name.

practical.title: Find my name
steps: Put three name cards on the floor.
Each child finds their own card.
Hold it up and say the name.
practical.safety: Make the cards smooth and laminated if possible. Return cards to their basket at the end.

differentiation.support: Keep the photo visible and point to the word with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a friend’s name card.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Finds their own name card with support
lessons.conclusion: Put the cards in the basket and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Write your child’s name on paper and look at it together.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find their own name card among three" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Print in books
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will notice print in books and point to words.
successCriteria: Points to words in a book
Says that the words tell the story
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can handle books, name pictures and recognise their own name card with a photo.
resources: A big book or a board book with large print
lessons.starter: Open a book and point to the words. Say "These are words. They tell us the story."
teacherActivities: Read a page and run your finger under the words.
Ask "Where are the words?" and wait.
Let each child point to the words on a page.
learnerActivities: Children look at the words and listen.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Read a page and run your finger under the words. Children: Children look at the words and listen.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Where are the words?" and wait. Children: Child points to the words.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Where is the picture?" Children: Child points to the picture.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child point to the words on a page. Children: Child points and friends watch.

practical.title: Words and pictures
steps: Open a big book on the floor.
Each child points to a picture and to the words.
practical.safety: Keep the book low so that everyone can see. Handle the book gently and sit with space.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to point to a long word and a short word.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Points to words in a book
Tells words from pictures with support
lessons.conclusion: Close the book and say "The end."
lessons.homeConnection: Run your finger under the words as you read to your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "notice print in books and point to words" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 9 print check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child notices print and finds their name card.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can handle books, name pictures and recognise their own name card with a photo.
lessons.starter: Say "Where are the words?" and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: signs, packets and name cards.
At each station ask "Where are the words?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: signs, packets and name cards. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "Where are the words?" Children: Child points to the print.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Print stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use clean, undamaged packets and signs.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use photo name cards.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to find a friend’s name card.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: points to print; says what a sign is for; finds their own name card among three.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 9
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say "We saw words everywhere."
lessons.homeConnection: Point out print around your home and read it aloud.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child notices print and finds their name card" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
